preamble: The vast question index. Each family is a catalog of typed typesafe.ai System One questions whose ANSWERS ARE the relational weights of the external mind. The oracle answers; the mechanical bot transcribes into nodes.csv/edges.csv. Specs are PRE-REGISTERED here (spec_sha over canon(spec)) before any round runs - the Wave-69 anti-post-hoc discipline. Expansion: families are instantiated over the lexicon and over the matrix's own labels, so the quilt grows questions from its own nodes.

families.description: Pairwise relational bond between two concepts. The root family: one batched typesafe call yields a fully weighted edge (joy from resonance probability, entropy from contradiction probability, value from a rubric).
families.state: Concept A: '{a}'. Concept B: '{b}'. Context: a growing web of ideas where relations carry joy/entropy/value weights.

resonates.instructions: Do '{a}' and '{b}' genuinely resonate - does thinking about one meaningfully light up the other?

contradicts.instructions: Do '{a}' and '{b}' contradict each other - are they hard to hold as fully true in the same web?

strength.instructions: How strong is the relation between '{a}' and '{b}'?

families.bind: rel_type = contradicts>0.6 ? contradicts : (resonates>0.5 ? resonates : echoes); joy=resonates; entropy=contradicts; value=strength_norm

families.description: Node fission. A small cell proposes 2-4 sub-ideas of a parent; the oracle weighs each sub on two gates (essential? distinct?). Passing subs become nodes with feeds-edges from the parent. This is how the web self-decomposes.
families.state: Parent concept: '{a}'. Its current paper (relations): {paper}. Proposed sub-idea: '{b}'.

essential.instructions: Is '{b}' an essential part or aspect of '{a}'?

distinct.instructions: Is '{b}' meaningfully distinct enough from '{a}' to deserve its own node?

families.bind: if essential>0.5 and distinct>0.5: add node b (joy=0.4+0.4*essential, entropy=0.5, value=essential) + edge a->b rel=feeds

families.description: Distant-cluster bridging. A cell proposes a connector concept C between distant A and B; the oracle judges whether C genuinely bridges and how strong the bridge is. Long-range structure is how a web stops being a hairball.
families.state: Concept A: '{a}'. Distant concept B: '{b}'. Proposed bridge concept C: '{c}'.

bridges.instructions: Does '{c}' genuinely bridge '{a}' and '{b}' - is it a real middle term, not a pun?

weight.instructions: How load-bearing is the bridge '{c}' between '{a}' and '{b}'?

families.bind: if bridges>0.5: ensure node c; edges a->c and c->b rel=bridges with value=weight_norm, joy=bridges

families.description: Self-audit of an existing edge. The oracle is asked whether a recorded relation is suspicious; a high suspicion scars the edge (sticky) and raises its entropy; a low suspicion confirms it (tiny value boost). The web that audits itself grows honest.

suspicious.instructions: Is this recorded relation suspicious - likely wrong, inflated, or a misreading of the pair?

repairable.instructions: If suspicious, how repairable is this relation by re-weighting alone?

families.bind: if suspicious>0.7: scar(reason=tension-audit, edge) + edge.entropy+=0.1; else edge.value+=0.02 (confirmed)

families.description: T-minus decomposition. A cell breaks a goal into an ordered countdown of stages; the oracle judges each adjacent pair with 'must X come before Y?'. Ordered dependency chains with weights - the t-minus paradigm as spreadsheet rows.
families.state: Goal: '{a}'. Stage X: '{b}'. Stage Y: '{c}'. Goal context: building '{a}' as a countdown sequence of stages.

before.instructions: Must stage '{b}' be completed before stage '{c}' on the way to '{a}'?

families.bind: if before>0.5: edge b->c rel=tminus value=0.8-pos*0.1 joy=before entropy=1-before

families.description: Sound parameters from a concept cluster. The oracle chooses a mode and scores brightness/density/velocity for the cluster; the mechanical bot writes sound.csv, and the music engine reads it. Music as a first-class output channel of the weights.

mode.instructions: Which musical mode best fits this cluster's character?

brightness.instructions: How bright is this cluster's character?

density.instructions: How dense/tangled are the ideas here?

velocity.instructions: How much energy should this cluster be played with?

families.bind: write sound.csv row {cluster, mode, brightness, density, velocity, round}; if brightness>0.6 also edge a->b rel=sounds

families.description: Moth-drifted neighbor probe. TRUE quantum bits (moth coin-toss-v1) pick an unexpected candidate neighbor for a concept; the oracle judges whether the drift is interesting. Quantum randomness as a creative act, receipted.
families.state: Concept A: '{a}'. Moth-drifted candidate neighbor: '{b}'. The candidate was chosen by a quantum coin (provenance {prov}).

fits.instructions: Is '{b}' a genuinely interesting neighbor for '{a}' - surprising but worth a tentative link?

families.bind: if fits>0.4: edge a->b rel=echoes joy=fits entropy=0.6+0.3*moth01 value=0.3 note=moth-drift

spec.fallback: deterministic hash pick, receipted sha: seed

families.description: Self-defending architecture. The oracle decides whether a node is load-bearing enough to deserve a guard spec; guarded nodes then REQUIRE provenance (question_id) on any future edge touching them - the mechanical gate refuses un-specced writes. Wave-69's spec gate, miniaturized.

needs_guard.instructions: Is '{a}' load-bearing enough in this web that edits touching it should require provenance?

guard_strength.instructions: How strict should the guard on '{a}' be?

families.bind: if needs_guard>0.5: guards.csv row {node, strength, round}; gate: new edges touching node without question_id -> scar(spec-missing)

families.description: Oracle self-consistency probe. The SAME relation question is asked twice with different phrasings; the delta between the two answers is the echo_delta. Large delta scars the pair as oracle-unstable; small delta confirms with a value boost. The unspoken-resonance lineage, instrumented.

p1.instructions: Do '{a}' and '{b}' belong close together in the same web?

p2.instructions: If you met '{a}' and '{b}' in a new unfinished idea-map, would you draw a line between them?

families.bind: delta=|p1-p2|; if delta>0.35: scar(oracle-instability, pair); else edge a->b rel=resonates value=0.5+0.3*(1-delta)

families.description: Play. The oracle chooses which micro-game two cells play over a pair this round, then judges whether the played pattern was joyful. Games are logged; joyful plays become plays-edges. Play is a first-class epistemic act, not a reward.
families.state: Cell X holds '{a}'. Cell Y holds '{b}'.

game.instructions: Which game should the cells play over this pair?

criteria.pass-the-note: one holds a tone, the other answers it
criteria.weight-auction: they bid joy/entropy/value for the edge
criteria.scar-tag: they try to tag each other's weakest weight
criteria.drone-drone: they hold sustained tones and listen for beats

fun.instructions: Was the pattern the cells produced joyful?

families.bind: games.csv row {a, b, game, round}; if fun>0.5: edge a->b rel=plays joy=fun value=0.4
